Heard.

2. By this petition, the petitioner seeks for quashing First Information Report('FIR') vide Crime No.
298/2023 registered with Police Station Jalandhar (Rural), Phillaur, Punjab for the offence
punishable under Sections 420, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
3.  It is the contention of the petitioners that petitioners are the partners of M/s.
Avani Foods which is registered at Nagpur, is engaged in manufacturing spray dried cheese powder.

The company of the petitioners received order at Nagpur from one M/s Cremica Food Industries Ltd. ('the said Company') for purchase of spray dried cheese powder and accordingly, the spray dried cheese powder of 17,000 k.g. was supplied from Nagpur to the said Company.
Later on, said company disputed the quality of spray dried cheese powder in last two consignments of 4,000 k.g. each returned the said two consignments.
After deducting said amount for returned 2 908 wp 883.23 goods, the bill was raised, but the said Company did not pay the consideration for goods.
The petitioners' company issued notice dated 07.02.2023, but no payment was made.
Therefore, the company of the petitioner approached to Facilitation Council established under the Micro, Small and Act, 2006.
Accordingly, the said Authority issued notice dated 11.05.2023 to the said Company to appear before it.

It is the contention of the petitioner that to avoid the payment, the Rajesh S/O Govinddas Rathi And Another vs State Of Punjab Thr. Pso, Ps Jalandhar ... on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161947600/
1 representative of the said Company got the civil dispute converted into criminal and he lodged First Information Report against the petitioners at Jalandhar (Rural), Phillur, Tah. Phillur, Dist.
Jalandhar (Panjab) for the offence punishable under Sections 420 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
3. It is the submission of learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that the order was placed by the said Company at Nagpur and goods were supplied from Nagpur itself, therefore the part of cause of action arose within the jurisdiction of this Court.

To buttress his submission, he placed reliance on the decision of the Supreme Court in case of Navinchandra N. Majithia Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, (2000) 7 SCC 640.

entities.text: Navinchandra N. Majithia Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, (2000) 7 SCC 640
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Wherein it has been held that in view of Clause (2) of Article 226 the power conferred on the High Courts under Article 226 could as well be exercised by any High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the territories within 3 908 wp 883.23 which "the cause of action, wholly or in part, arises" and it is no matter that the seat of the authority concerned is outside the territorial limits of the jurisdiction of that High Court.
The Fifteenth Amendment of the Constitution which introduced clause (2) is thus aimed at widening the area for reaching the writs issued by different High Courts.

In view of peculiar facts of this case and keeping the point of jurisdiction opened, we pass the following order:-
(I). Issue notice to the respondents returnable after six weeks.
The learned APP waives service of notice for respondent No.3.

(II) No coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners by the respondent No.1.
till next date.
